doc.title: Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Oneonta, New York, December 28, 2005

title: Vaudeville acts seen from the Orpheum pit: Hope, Berle, Canovas, Cardini
summary: Names the acts he played for from the pit, and magician Cardini with his lit cigarettes.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: I’m curious about some of the vaudeville acts that you played for. Did you get to — could you see them performing while you were playing or were you in the pit?

Yes. We were in a pit, but we could look up on the stage. Bob Hope, he played his act twice, around 1930 and then he came back in ’31. Milton Berle. The Ritz Brothers. They were famous. The Canovas — Judy, Zeke and Ann. Two sisters and a brother. Not Houdini.
Yeah. A big magician, I think his son — I can’t think of his name at the moment, not Jackson — or Cardini.
Cardini uses to come on with lit cigarettes from all over. I never figured out how he did it.
